title: postmortem-draft-smart-routing-diverge
content:
Background:

This is a personal draft for a short-form postmortem / breadcrumbs log of the March 9th regional divergence where a subset of requests were steered away from the primary region and experienced extra token latency then saw degraded cache hits. Goal: capture commands I ran, snippets from logs, hypotheses to test, and a minimal reproduction plan before turning into a formal write-up.

High-level symptom:
- ~03:10-03:45 UTC on 2026-03-09 a spike in 95th/99th token latency for customers pinned to model: rdl/llama-70b-quant-v2 in us-west-2.
- Percent of requests that were routed to us-east-1 increased from ~0.4% baseline to ~6% for affected routes.
- Observed decrease in prefix/KV cache hit rate for those diverted requests (cache-hit-rate from ~82% -> ~21% on the us-east cold path).
- Autoscale and dedicated pools in us-west reported no CPU/GPU saturation; the steering decision was triggered by smart-routing policy.

Quick timeline I reconstructed:
- 03:07 UTC: control-plane note: pool-us-west2 reported transient RPC errors to backend (RPC_TYPE=BatchAlloc, 503).
- 03:08:21 UTC: smart-router policy evaluated circuit-breaker for us-west route (latency metric window=30s).
- 03:09:02 UTC: policy decision recorded: prefer-safety-tier -> divert to fallback region us-east-1 for 5% of traffic for routes with sample tag:tariff-E.
- 03:10-03:12 UTC: surge of diverted requests; us-east cold cache churn resulted.
- 03:20 UTC: operator override attempt (rollback diverted percentage) but policy engine re-applied rules.
- 03:44 UTC: routing policy auto-decay lowered diversion back to baseline after metrics normalized.

Commands and quick outputs (what I ran):

1) Query routing decisions for a single request id (replay):
- curl -sS -H "X-Req-Id: abc-10712" https://router.internal/api/v1/decision?id=abc-10712
  -> decision: route->us-east-1, reason=[policy:region-safety,score=0.78], cache_tag=kv_v2:rdl-llama-70b-window-1024

2) Check policy engine logs around 03:07-03:12 UTC (k logs):
- kubectl -n routing logs deploy/policy-engine -c engine --since-time=2026-03-09T03:00:00Z | grep "divert" -n | sed -n '1,120p'
  -> [03:08:21Z] INFO evaluate policy for route tariff-E window=30s latency_p95=342ms threshold=300ms -> action=divert pct=5
  -> [03:09:01Z] INFO commit diversion pct=5; plan=regional-safety-v3

3) Confirm backend RPC transient errors:
- kubectl -n serving logs deploy/pool-us-west2 -c server --since=1h | jq '.level=="error"' | head
  -> repeated 503: "batch allocator exhausted on worker-87" at 03:06:52, 03:07:04, 03:07:28

4) KV cache metrics:
- curl "https://metrics.internal/api/query?m=cache_hit_rate&pool=us-east-1&model=rdl/llama-70b-quant-v2&from=2026-03-09T02:50:00Z&to=2026-03-09T04:00:00Z"
  -> summary: pre-event=0.82, during=0.21, post=0.79

Error snippets captured from serving logs (copied as-is):
- "2026-03-09T03:06:52Z ERROR batch_alloc.cpp:112: batch request rejected - allocator exhausted; inflight=2048 limit=2000"
- "2026-03-09T03:07:04Z WARN kv_cache.cpp:441: eviction spike triggered, reclaimed 6 entries at once"
- "2026-03-09T03:09:11Z INFO router.cpp:277: routed id=abc-10712 -> us-east-1 (policy=regional-safety-v3)"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Primary cause: transient batch allocator exhaustion in us-west pools caused the policy engine to interpret increased latency/error rate as systemic and to divert traffic. That diversion then made the diverted requests hit cold KV caches in us-east which amplified token latency.
2) Contributing factor: policy threshold values (latency_p95 threshold=300ms) were tuned for full-capacity pools; transient allocator exhaustion (short-lived) should have been filtered by a second-level debounce or by looking at backend pool saturation metrics (GPU utilization) instead of allocator errors.
3) Edge case: TTLs for cross-region KV replication were marginally off; when diverting, KV key absence was higher than expected because replication lag for recently warmed prefixes was ~45s due to network jitter on the inter-region replication pipeline.
4) Operator flow: the operator rollback happened but the policy engine re-evaluated and re-applied the diversion because the underlying allocator errors still appeared; lack of coordinated operator lockout allowed re-application.

Immediate mitigation steps I tried (notes):
- Increased batch allocator limit on pool-us-west2 instance group by +10% (temporary config tweak) -> reduced 503s; observed allocator errors stop after ~120s.
- Pushed a temporary policy patch to policy-engine to treat "allocator_exhausted" as low-severity for the next 60s (debounce window). This was a quick patch: PR #4578 (linked above).
- Manually primed KV in us-east for top-50 failing prefixes (used a mini-batch replay against a mirror pipeline). Priming reduced p95 for diverted requests by ~90ms during the window.

Reproduction plan (minimal):
1) On staging: set pool-a to have allocator limit N and artificially generate small bursts of concurrent batch requests to trigger allocator-exhausted logs.
2) Ensure policy-engine threshold matches production config (latency_p95=300ms) and observe whether it diverts to pool-b.
3) Measure KV cold-hit penalty by diverting requests with intentionally absent KV prefixes and timing tokens.
4) Verify operator disable prevents policy re-application by toggling operator flag.

Open action items (what to include in final PM):
- Short-term: Add a 60s debounce on policy triggers that originate from allocator_exhausted error class (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
- Short-term: Change policy evaluation to include GPU_utilization < 90% as an override condition before diverting (owner: eng-platform-routing).
- Medium-term: Improve KV cross-region replication: instrument observed replication lag per-prefix and set alert when >10s for hot prefixes (owner: eng-infra).
- Medium-term: Add a canary pipeline to pre-warm KV in possible fallback regions for top-N prefixes per-customer (owner: eng-optimize).
- Ops: Add a temporary dashboard tile showing diversion_pct by route and associated cache_hit_rate so on-call can correlate quickly.

Notes to self / unresolved questions:
- Did the allocator-exhausted events originate from a single worker type or spread across the entire us-west deployment? I saw worker-87 in logs but need to look at node-level metrics to confirm whether this was localized.
- The operator rollback attempt: why did it not flip a global operator lock? Need to check operator flow and whether policy-engine honors operator lockouts.
- Are there other error classes that cause similar blind diversions? E.g., qps spikes, partial RPC latency, or intermittent datastore timeouts.

Scratch commands to run next time I pick this up:
- kubectl -n serving top pod pool-us-west2-pod-87 --containers
- curl "https://router.internal/api/v1/decision?id=abc-10712&trace=1" | jq '.'
- kafka-console-consumer --topic policy-events --from-beginning --max-messages 500 --property print.key=true | grep "regional-safety" -n
- python tools/kv_primer.py --region us-east-1 --model rdl/llama-70b-quant-v2 --prefix-file top50.txt

Endnotes: this is rough. Will convert to a short exec summary if we agree on the hypothesis ranking. If anyone reading wants me to drop into SRE rotation to run the reproduction, ping me and I'll slot it.

-- Asha
